newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down 2.48 pct on rate concerns.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down 2.48 pct on rate concerns.

text.p: Concerns over high commercial bank interest rates forced investors to sell Thai stocks on Thursday, driving the market down by 2.48 percent in moderate trade, brokers said.
The composite SET index closed 14.80 points lower to 581.39 on 5.6 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index dropped 1.51 points to 42.36.

"Investors, including foreigners, sold and took profits today as they watched whether the central bank would lower its discount rate or not. They believed that commercial banks would cut their rates if the central bank cut the discount rate," said Kasem Prunratanamala of James Capel Asia.
Thai Bankers Association chief Olarn Chaiprawat said on Wednesday the Bank of Thailand was likely to cut its discount rate in the coming days to trigger interest rates cuts by commercial banks.
But the central bank has not said when it will drop the rate although the finance ministry has hinted a cut is on the way.
Brokers said they believed a market support fund continued buying for the second day.
However they said the support fund, which commercial banks would pool in a total of 50 billion baht to help shore up the market, was less active on Thursday than on Wednesday.
"I think foreigners continued selling today with an aim to cut their losses," said Kasem.
Total net selling by foreigners on Wednesday amounted to 434 million baht.
Decliners trounced gainers 222 to 97 while 72 issues were unchanged.

Most of the key sectors declined on Thursday with the banking sector falling the most in terms of value, declining 4.90 percent, followed by the communication sector which retreated 1.78 percent. The finance sector fell 4.19 percent.
Krung Thai Bank topped the active list in terms of value, falling 1.75 baht to 30. Advanced Info Services shed one to 174 and National Finance retreated 2.75 to 24.75.
